requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature. It MUST direct them to review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all the reviews running in parallel, before presenting any group to the user.
rationale:
The test adequately checks every obligation in the requirement. It is marked `{test}` for it.

The requirement has two parts, and the skill text is the deliverable. The skill is `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, under Workflow, step 3 (Review) and step 4 (Present each group to the user).

**Grouping.** The skill MUST direct agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group of requirements that cite each other or describe one feature.
- `the_requirements_skill_reviews_each_group_with_a_parallel_read_only_subagent` finds the step containing "start a read-only subagent". It does this with `step_of`, which fails if no step contains the phrase.
- It then takes that step's text, collapsed across its continuation lines by `workflow_steps`/`collapse`. It asserts the text contains "Sort the new and changed requirements into groups" and "requirements that cite each other or describe one feature".
- That covers the grouping obligation and the group definition. The step text does contain these phrases.

**Review.** The skill MUST direct agents to review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all reviews in parallel, before presenting any group.
- The test asserts the step contains "For each group, start a read-only subagent, all in parallel". That covers every group, its own subagent, read-only, and parallel.
- The test asserts `review < step_of(SKILL, "Present each group to the user")`. That covers the ordering, "before presenting any group".

**Assessment.** The skill is documentation, so asserting its exact directive phrases and step ordering is the right way to test it. I found no input class or boundary the requirement names that the test misses. `workflow_steps` is exercised by sibling tests, and I read it to confirm its parsing.

The SKILL.md text I read matches every asserted phrase, so the assertions would pass and would fail if the directives were removed or reordered. Other tests in the file (`home_markers`, `bundled_skills_say_when_to_read_each_reference_file`) also pin the same phrases, which gives extra protection.
